interest: This file offers a revealing glimpse into mounting pre-World War II strategic tensions and local friction surrounding Japanese naval presence in the Hawaiian Islands. It highlights the interdepartmental policy effort to restrict Japanese government vessels strictly to Honolulu and bar them from outlying Hawaiian ports, underscoring American defense anxieties in the Pacific. Additionally, the incident involving the Japanese naval tanker Hayatome and the Mutual Telephone Company illustrates how local commercial entities reacted to perceived misconduct or security breaches by Japanese sailors, escalating civil friction into interagency diplomatic correspondence.
overview: This file consists of a Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (decimal file 894.3311A) tracking correspondence and memoranda from late 1937 and 1938 concerning the visits of Japanese government and naval vessels to ports in Hawaii. The entries summarize policy recommendations formulated by an interdepartmental committee to the President to deny Japanese public vessels access to all Hawaiian ports with the exception of Honolulu. The docket also records a June 1938 incident in Honolulu involving the Japanese naval tanker Hayatome, where mistreatment of a Mutual Telephone Company employee led the company to refuse future service to Japanese ships without an apology, prompting coordination between the Navy Department and the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs.

subfiles.summary: This document is the official State Department list of papers cataloguing documents filed under decimal number 894.3311A between November 1937 and June 1938. The first sub-entry summarizes a memorandum by Assistant Secretary Hugh R. Wilson stating that Japanese public vessels will only be permitted to visit Honolulu and instructing consultation with the Far Eastern Division on related communications from the Japanese Embassy. Subsequent entries document Navy Department communications concerning the Japanese naval tanker Hayatome at Honolulu, specifically a dispute with the Mutual Telephone Company over the discourteous treatment of an employee by Japanese sailors and the company's refusal to provide further telephone installations without an apology.
